reports.title: Eurostat Intermediate Report
reports.description: A twice-cycle companion to the annual Eurostat Remuneration Report, updating Intra-EU correction-coefficient inputs between full annual recalculations. Eurostat's own Publications page: 'Reports are typically released in May with reference date January' (ERR-05). Titled from the series' own file metadata -- 'Eurostat_Intermediate_Report_[year]' -- confirmed across 14 linked years (2013-2026).
reports.cadence_note: Eurostat Publications page: 'Reports are typically released in May with reference date January' (ERR-05) -- a distinct reference date and release month from the annual report (which reports as at July, released late October).

reports.title: Eurostat Report on the Interim Update of Weightings (Correction Coefficients) for Extra-EU Delegations
reports.description: Named in full at footnote 3, item 2 of COM(2025) 736 (C736-04, EU/AnnexXI_PartA_2026-08-05.md): 'Eurostat Reports of 3 June 2025 and 31 October 2025 on the interim update of weightings (correction coefficients) applicable to the remuneration of officials, temporary staff and contract staff of the European Union serving in Extra-EU Delegations in accordance with Article 64 and Annex X and Annex XI of the Staff Regulations...' Eurostat's own Publications page confirms the twice-yearly pattern generalises across years and lists 15 years of paired releases (2011-2026).
reports.cadence_note: Eurostat Publications page: 'Reports are typically released in May with reference date January, and in October with reference date July' (ERR-06). C736-04 dates the 2025 pair as 3 June and 31 October.

reports.title: Estate Agency Rent Surveys (EARS)
reports.description: Eurostat's own Methodology page: 'Estate agency rent surveys (EARS) are done in the context of the wider work done to compare the relative cost of living of international civil servants between their place of employment and that of Brussels, the reference city. Because of the importance of housing costs in the overall expenditure of a household, specific rent surveys are carried out annually through estate agencies.' (ERR-07). Publications page lists 23 linked years (2003-2025).
reports.cadence_note: Eurostat Methodology page: 'specific rent surveys are carried out annually through estate agencies' (ERR-07), confirmed by 23 consecutive linked years on the Publications page.

entries.covers: Rents booklet with June 2026 average rent prices (survey collected mid-2026, published autumn 2026)

release_schedule.rule: Estate agency rent surveys (EARS) are carried out annually. Per Eurostat's ESMS metadata (prc_colc_rents_esms): Frequency of dissemination = "Yearly". Timeliness: "Average rent prices for June (1st July) are published in autumn of the same year." Punctuality: "There is no formal requirement to publish average rent prices on a specific date, however publication takes place as quickly as possible after the publication of the Eurostat Annual remuneration report and finalisation of the annual booklet on current market rents."
release_schedule.note: No fixed calendar date exists; the publisher states only that the annual rents booklet (based on June rent data) appears 'in autumn of the same year', following the related Eurostat Annual Remuneration Report. The computed entry approximates autumn (Sept-Nov) 2026 since today (2026-08-11) precedes that window; actual date within autumn is not published in advance.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat Methodology page, 'Correction coefficients' section (ERR-07): 'For housing, which is the largest single item of expenditure for many people, a specific methodology has been set up and constantly improved over time by Eurostat with the national statistical institutes. Rent parities are based on market rents obtained from special surveys of estate agencies.' 'Based on' is a direct input statement, not a Research.1.md §5a 'comparable with' trap. Housing/rent parities are part of the correction-coefficient calculation that feeds the annual report's own arithmetic (Methodology page, Correction coefficients formula section).

_dropped.why: Investigated as candidate nodes and found, from their own file names retrieved via the Publications page's DOM, to be Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 of the same annual 'Eurostat Remuneration Report [year]' already minted as eurostat-remuneration-update-report -- not an independent series. See ERR-08, EU/EurostatRemunerationReport_PartA_2026-08-05.md. Not minted, per the measured part_of/double-counting finding documented in src/lib/types.ts (Report.part_of): splitting a component from its parent release understates the parent's authority rather than adding information.
